title: 魏尔斯特拉斯的怪物：连续却处处不可微

claims.statement: 1872 Weierstrass presented a continuous nowhere differentiable function; 1875 du Bois-Reymond published relevant work
claims.locator: year and du Bois-Reymond 1875 vol 79 pp21-37

claims.statement: Bolzano's pre-1834 manuscript contains earlier construction, printed 1930, original dense non-differentiability proof distinguished from later global result
Riemann 1861 earlier unpublished suggestions debated; cannot infer complete contemporary proof
claims.locator: scholarly historical account with cautious attribution

claims.statement: continuity does not imply differentiation; |x| not differentiable at 0
classical W(x)=Σa^n cos(π b^n x) with a∈(0,1), b odd integer and ab>1+3π/2 is continuous nowhere differentiable
claims.locator: classical sufficient conditions in math research

claims.statement: W series uniformly absolutely converges with tail bound Σ_{n>N}2^-n=2^-N
uniform limit of continuous finite cosine sums continuous on R

claims.locator: all cosine differences at maximum nonpositive and m-th term -2·2^-m

claims.statement: x=0 difference quotient only proves nondifferentiability at 0, not every point
claims.locator: full theorem sourced separately; explicit method limitation

claims.statement: formal termwise derivative series divergence does not entail failure of derivative of the sum
claims.locator: interchange of limit and derivative requires hypotheses

claims.statement: W continuous on closed bounded intervals hence Riemann integrable despite nowhere differentiable
smoothness not equivalent to integrability; next Darboux upper and lower sums

caveats: Bolzano1834/1930 separates priority and publication; original Bolzano dense nondifferentiability proof and later full theorem distinguish.
Weierstrass1872 presentation vs du Bois-Reymond1875 print distinguished.
Chosen a=.5 b=13 is present-day example not specifically Weierstrass 1872 chosen constants.
Difference quotient at x=0 not a complete proof of nowhere differentiability; cite full standard theorem.
Neither divergent formal derivative series nor rough image substitutes a proof.
